title: Target Configuration Synthesis
description: You are given a list of component configurations represented as integer triplets, where triplets[i] = [a_i, b_i, c_i], and a target configuration target = [x, y, z]. In one operation, you can choose two or more triplets and combine their attributes component-wise by taking the maximum value for each position across the chosen triplets. Determine if it is possible to synthesize the exact target configuration by performing this operation any number of times.
input_format: A 2D integer array triplets and an integer array target.

examples.explanation: Choose the first and second triplets. Taking the max per position gives [max(2,1), max(5,8), max(3,4)] = [2, 8, 4]. Wait, we need [2, 8, 5], which can be obtained by choosing [2, 5, 3], [1, 8, 4], and [1, 7, 5]. Max of elements gives [2, 8, 5].

No triplet can have any component greater than the target's respective component if we want to avoid exceeding the target. Here, the first component of the target is 3, but the second triplet has 4, which is fine, but we can't get y=2 when elements have higher values.
Combining the relevant triplets yields the target [5, 5, 5].
